input: Research standing desks for under two hundred dollars

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Standing desks vary widely — full desks, desktop risers, and converter units are all options. Knowing which type is wanted narrows research dramatically.
The desk may be for the user alone or shared; a child, adult, or tall person has very different height and size requirements.
Whether it goes in a home office, corporate office, or small apartment affects size, aesthetics, and assembly requirements.
Beyond budget, there may be hard limits on desk footprint, weight capacity, or available floor/desk space that would rule out many options.
Some users prioritize ease of height adjustment (electric vs. manual vs. fixed), while others care about surface material or style — this shapes which models to focus on.
The output of this research could be a shortlist, a single recommendation, a comparison table, or a buying guide — knowing what 'done' looks like determines how deep to go.
Knowing the preferred shopping channel (Amazon, local stores, specific retailers) and whether assembly is acceptable affects which products are even viable.

gold.taskTitle: Research standing desks under two hundred dollars
gold.taskDescription: Find and evaluate standing desk options available for under $200 to support a purchase decision.

questions.title: Which type of standing desk do you want — full desk, desktop riser, or converter?
questions.description: Identifies whether the user wants a freestanding desk that replaces their current one, a riser that sits on top of an existing desk, or another format entirely.

questions.title: Who will be using this desk primarily?
questions.description: Determines the user's height, usage habits, and whether the desk needs to accommodate more than one person, which affects height range and surface size requirements.

questions.title: Where in your space will this desk be placed?
questions.description: Establishes the physical environment — home office, bedroom, open-plan office — which influences size, weight, and aesthetic needs.

questions.title: Is there a maximum footprint or surface size the desk must fit within?
questions.description: Captures any hard spatial constraints such as a specific wall width, corner placement, or maximum depth that would eliminate certain models.

questions.title: Do you prefer electric height adjustment, a manual crank, or a fixed height?
questions.description: Pinpoints the adjustment mechanism preference, which is one of the biggest differentiators in price and usability within a sub-$200 budget.

questions.title: What should the final research output look like — a shortlist, one top pick, or a comparison table?
questions.description: Defines what a successful research result actually is, so the depth and format of the output matches the user's real need.

questions.title: Which retailers or shopping channels should the search focus on?
questions.description: Narrows sourcing to preferred stores such as Amazon, IKEA, Wayfair, or local retailers, and flags whether shipping time or in-store pickup matters.
